page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the architecture is x86_64. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or a GPU, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance, contrasted by weak single-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 12409.56, placing it in the average tier, while its single-core score of 779.18 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only large block speeds at 48.36 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 28.85 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak at 7.69 GB/sec, though multi-threaded decompression reaches an average speed of 149.14 GB/sec. For database and memory operations, the server achieves average scores, with a PassMark database operations score of 9717.18 and Redis SET operations performing at 22.55 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation and poor single-core performance, which limits its utility for single-threaded or latency-sensitive workloads. However, its 96.0 GB memory capacity and 16 physical cores offer a resource-dense profile for multi-threaded tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model provides a budget-friendly path to high-memory configurations without the premium of dedicated compute. This server is suitable for multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, Redis caching, database operations, and light multi-threaded data processing where single-core speed is not critical.
